scope: Independent read-only code review and host-only tests; no SSH, device, hardware, build or frozen-source edits

findings.finding: No device access is needed for keyboard opt-in validation, and production callers validate it before orderly reboot and before serial open. It requires exact fixed command/version, a verified RAM-root artifact, no desktop experiment, a native fileset, and exactly one SPI HID member.

normal_image verifies every artifact size/SHA256 and the completed build record, then structurally inspects the KC. The keyboard helper adds only pdm1kbd=1; all original board/proxy/MMIO/recovery checks remain in the existing path. Actual final kext source fidelity and 51-member KC inspection are root-owned pending evidence.

Inventory uses the matching minimal PDIOKitLib string-based ABI and its static library; matching calls are sequential so the static XML buffer is not reused concurrently. The source contains no IOServiceOpen, HID queue open, ioctl or input injection; device checks are stat only.

Guest launcher validates a 48-hex nonce, runs inventory, then blocks reading the literal human line m1keyboard. It emits DLK_TYPED only after an exact read match. No host code supplies this line or SOH virtual-HID input; the host sends only the fixed launcher after an independently verified Darwin shell challenge.

Controller status/exit success means Darwin CLI plus Linux recovery, not keyboard success. Inventory presence and an initial native report can include idle/release reports and are insufficient to prove human typing. Preserve this distinction in the hardware receipt.
findings.action: Require the raw DLK_READY then DLK_TYPED nonce sequence, the real driver input-delivery observation, artifact/launch binding, and human confirmation of built-in-keyboard typing and visible response before claiming native input.

findings.finding: PDIOKitLib IOIteratorNext collapses iterator RPC errors to IO_OBJECT_NULL, the same sentinel as exhaustion. Therefore query_errors:false is not proof that every service enumeration completed without an RPC error; counts are a bounded observation, not exhaustive absence proof. No native-keyboard success claim is made by the tool.
